Built by an interdisciplinary team of data scientists, investigative journalists, and social researchers, the Institute develops evidence-based tools and strategies to detect, analyse, and reduce the spread of false or misleading information across digital platforms.\n",
        "\n",
        "**Key Focus Areas:**\n",
        "- **Data-Driven Research** — Mining large-scale datasets to uncover linguistic and behavioural patterns unique to misinformation\n",
        "- **Automated Detection** — Deploying machine learning models to flag potentially false content at scale\n",
        "- **Digital Literacy Programmes** — Equipping the public and institutions with frameworks for critical media consumption\n",
        "- **Policy Advisory** — Providing evidence-backed guidance to governments and media organisations on information governance\n",

      "source": [
        "---\n",
        "# STEP 1: PROJECT OVERVIEW\n",
        "\n",
        "The proliferation of fake news poses a measurable threat to public discourse, democratic institutions, and organisational trust. The TruthLens Institute has engaged us as **Lead Data Scientists** to design and evaluate a machine learning pipeline that classifies news articles as **fake** or **real** using their textual content alone.\n",
        "\n",
        "> *Can we reliably predict, from the linguistic content of a news article, whether it is real or fabricated — and identify which words and phrases are the strongest signals of each class?*\n",
        "\n",
        "---\n",
        "\n",
        "## 1.1 Project Workflow\n",
        "\n",
        "| Step | Phase | Description |\n",
        "|------|-------|-------------|\n",
        "| **1** | Project Overview | Objectives, business problem, and workflow |\n",
        "| **2** | Data Loading & Cleaning | Load the 20-column dataset, inspect all columns, clean and standardise text |\n",
        "| **3** | Feature Engineering | Binary label mapping, class balancing, numerical features, TF-IDF matrix |\n",
        "| **4** | Model Development & Evaluation | Train five classifiers, evaluate on five metrics, compare via ROC-AUC |\n",
        "| **5** | Hyperparameter Tuning | GridSearchCV tuning of the two best-performing baseline models |\n",
        "| **6** | Business Insights & Recommendations | Key findings, model recommendation, actionable guidance, limitations |\n",
        "\n",
        "---\n",
        "\n",
        "## 1.2 Dataset Context\n",
        "\n",
        "This project uses the **LIAR / OpenSources-style dataset** — a real-world collection of 12,999 news articles crawled from various sources between 2015 and 2016. Unlike simple binary-labelled benchmarks, this dataset contains **8 fine-grained misinformation categories** (`bs`, `bias`, `conspiracy`, `hate`, `satire`, `state`, `junksci`, `fake`) plus engagement metadata (likes, shares, comments) and publication details.\n",
        "\n",
        "A key analytical decision in this project is the **binary label mapping strategy**: collapsing the 8 categories into `fake` and `real`, then addressing the resulting severe class imbalance through downsampling.\n",
        "\n",
        "---\n",
        "\n",
        "## 1.3 Deliverables\n",
        "\n",
        "1. Complete data inspection of a 20-column real-world dataset with 11,229 total missing values\n",
        "2. Justified binary label mapping from 8 multi-class categories\n",
        "3. Cleaned, preprocessed NLP pipeline (text normalisation, lemmatisation, TF-IDF)\n",
        "4. Engineered features: `word_count`, `sentiment` (VADER), TF-IDF (20,000 features, unigrams + bigrams)\n",
        "5. Comparative evaluation of five classifiers across five metrics\n",
        "6. GridSearchCV-tuned best model with ROC-AUC validation\n",
        "7. Feature importance analysis identifying the lexical drivers of fake vs real news\n",
        "8. Serialised production model\n",
        "\n",
        "---"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",

        "\n",
        "The 20-column structure of this dataset — far richer than a simple labelled text file — requires careful column selection, missing value analysis, and a considered strategy for the multi-class target variable.\n",

        "### E. Text Normalisation — `clean_text()`\n",
        "\n",
        "Raw text contains noise that dilutes the discriminative signal available for classification: special characters, digits, punctuation, high-frequency function words (stopwords), and morphological variants of the same root (e.g., `running`, `runs`, `ran` all reduce to `run`). We define a `clean_text()` function that applies a five-stage normalisation pipeline to every article.\n",
        "\n",
        "**Five-Stage Pipeline:**\n",
        "\n",
        "| Stage | Operation | Purpose |\n",
        "|-------|-----------|---------|\n",
        "| 1 | Remove special characters and digits | Retains only alphabetic characters |\n",
        "| 2 | Lowercase conversion | Eliminates case-based duplicates (`Trump` = `trump`) |\n",
        "| 3 | Punctuation removal | Strips remaining non-alphabetic symbols |\n",
        "| 4 | Tokenisation | Splits text into individual word tokens |\n",
        "| 5 | Stopword removal + Lemmatisation | Removes uninformative function words; reduces tokens to dictionary root form |\n",
        "\n",
        "**Why lemmatisation over stemming?** Lemmatisation produces valid English words (`running → run`), not truncated fragments (`running → runn`). This preserves interpretability in the TF-IDF feature space and in the feature importance analysis."
      ]
    },

        "# ── Initialise NLP components ─────────────────────────────────────────────────\n",
        "stop_words  = set(stopwords.words('english'))\n",
        "lemmatizer  = WordNetLemmatizer()\n",
        "\n",
        "# ── Define the five-stage text normalisation function ─────────────────────────\n",
        "def clean_text(text):\n",
        "    if not isinstance(text, str):\n",
        "        return ''\n",
        "\n",
        "    # ── Stage 1: Remove special characters and digits ─────────────────────────\n",
        "    sentence = re.sub('[^a-zA-Z]', ' ', text)\n",
        "\n",
        "    # ── Stage 2: Lowercase conversion ─────────────────────────────────────────\n",
        "    sentence = sentence.lower()\n",
        "\n",
        "    # ── Stage 3: Punctuation removal ──────────────────────────────────────────\n",
        "    sentence = ''.join([char for char in sentence if char not in string.punctuation])\n",
        "\n",
        "    # ── Stage 4: Tokenisation ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n",
        "    tokens = sentence.split()\n",
        "\n",
        "    # ── Stage 5: Stopword removal + Lemmatisation ─────────────────────────────\n",
        "    clean_tokens = [lemmatizer.lemmatize(word) for word in tokens if word not in stop_words]\n",
        "\n",
        "    return ' '.join(clean_tokens)\n",
        "\n",
        "print(\"✓ clean_text() function defined. Applying to 'content' column...\")\n",
        "df['content'] = df['content'].apply(clean_text)\n",
        "print(\"✓ Text normalisation complete.\")\n",
        "df.head(3)"
      ]

        "---\n",
        "# STEP 3: FEATURE ENGINEERING\n",
        "\n",
        "With a clean dataset in hand, we now construct the feature representation that models will learn from. This step has five components, each building on the previous:\n",
        "\n",
        "1. **Numerical features** — `word_count` and `sentiment` score from each article\n",
        "2. **Text visualisation** — WordClouds by category and top bigram analysis\n",
        "3. **Binary label mapping** — collapsing 8 categories into `fake` / `real` with justification\n",
        "4. **Class balancing** — downsampling to address the 29.8:1 imbalance after mapping\n",
        "5. **TF-IDF matrix construction** — 20,000-feature sparse representation combining unigrams and bigrams\n",
        "\n",

        "## 3.1 Numerical Feature Extraction\n",
        "\n",
        "Before applying the binary label mapping, we engineer two numerical features across all 12,720 records. These features capture article-level properties that supplement the lexical TF-IDF signal:\n",
        "\n",
        "- **`word_count`** — the number of clean tokens after normalisation. Different misinformation types may exhibit systematic differences in verbosity (e.g., `bs` articles may be shorter than `conspiracy` articles).\n",
        "- **`sentiment`** — the VADER compound score, ranging from −1.0 (most negative) to +1.0 (most positive). VADER is specifically calibrated for social media and news-style text, making it well-suited to this dataset."

        "# ── Initialise VADER sentiment analyser ──────────────────────────────────────\n",
        "sia = SentimentIntensityAnalyzer()\n",
        "\n",
        "# ── Engineer word_count feature ───────────────────────────────────────────────\n",
        "df['word_count'] = df['content'].str.split().str.len()\n",
        "\n",
        "# ── Engineer sentiment feature ────────────────────────────────────────────────\n",
        "df['sentiment']  = df['content'].apply(lambda x: sia.polarity_scores(x)['compound'])\n",
        "\n",
        "print(\"✓ Numerical features engineered: 'word_count' and 'sentiment'.\")\n",
        "print(f\"  word_count  — min: {df['word_count'].min():,}  |  max: {df['word_count'].max():,}  |  mean: {df['word_count'].mean():.1f}\")\n",
        "print(f\"  sentiment   — min: {df['sentiment'].min():.4f}  |  max: {df['sentiment'].max():.4f}  |  mean: {df['sentiment'].mean():.4f}\")\n",

        "**Key findings from numerical feature engineering:**\n",
        "- **`word_count`** ranges from **0 to 4,444 tokens**, with a mean of **351.1 tokens** per article. The range of 0 reflects articles where the `title` and `text` fields were both empty — these records contribute nothing to classification and are effectively filtered by the TF-IDF vectoriser.\n",
        "- **`sentiment`** spans the full VADER range from **−1.000 to +1.000**, with a near-neutral mean of **+0.028**. The near-zero mean confirms that the overall corpus is tonally neutral in aggregate — neither systematically positive nor negative — which means sentiment alone cannot reliably discriminate fake from real content. Its value lies in capturing extreme outliers within each class.\n",
        "\n",
        "These two features supplement the TF-IDF matrix by encoding properties of the article as a whole, rather than the presence or absence of specific terms.\n",

        "## 3.3 Binary Label Mapping — A Critical Design Decision\n",
        "\n",
        "The project objective requires binary classification (`fake` / `real`). The 8 raw categories must be mapped to this binary target. This is the most analytically important decision in the entire pipeline, as it determines both the signal the model receives and the class distribution it must navigate.\n",
        "\n",
        "**Mapping Rationale:**\n",
        "\n",
        "| Original Category | Mapped To | Justification |\n",
        "|-------------------|-----------|---------------|\n",
        "| `bs` | **fake** | Broadly unreliable, low-quality misinformation — the core \"fake\" content type |\n",
        "| `conspiracy` | **fake** | Unsubstantiated claims designed to mislead |\n",
        "| `hate` | **fake** | Disinformation framed as news to incite |\n",
        "| `satire` | **fake** | Intentionally fictional, often mistaken for real |\n",
        "| `state` | **fake** | State-sponsored propaganda — deliberately deceptive |\n",
        "| `junksci` | **fake** | Pseudoscience presented as fact |\n",
        "| `fake` | **fake** | Explicitly fabricated news |\n",
        "| `bias` | **real** | Ideologically slanted but reporting on real events — the closest available proxy for \"real\" news in this dataset |\n",
        "\n",
        "**Important caveat:** The `bias` category is not truly \"real\" news in the sense of being factually verified. It represents partisan but grounded reporting. This mapping is a pragmatic choice given the dataset's structure — and is acknowledged as a limitation in Step 6."
      ]
    },

        "# ── Plot the top 15 bigrams for each binary class ────────────────────────────\n",
        "def plot_top_ngrams(texts, n=2, label_category='fake', top_n=15):\n",
        "    vec = CountVectorizer(ngram_range=(n, n), stop_words='english').fit(texts)\n",
        "    bag_of_words = vec.transform(texts)\n",
        "    sum_words    = bag_of_words.sum(axis=0)\n",
        "    words_freq   = [(word, sum_words[0, idx]) for word, idx in vec.vocabulary_.items()]\n",
        "    words_freq   = sorted(words_freq, key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)[:top_n]\n",
        "    x_vals, y_vals = zip(*words_freq)\n",
        "\n",
        "    plt.figure(figsize=(11, 5))\n",
        "    sns.barplot(x=list(y_vals), y=list(x_vals), palette='Set2')\n",
        "    plt.title(f'Top {top_n} Bigrams — {label_category.upper()} Articles',\n",
        "              fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')\n",
        "    plt.xlabel('Frequency')\n",
        "    plt.ylabel('Bigram')\n",
        "    plt.tight_layout()\n",
        "    plt.savefig(f'bigrams_{label_category}.png', dpi=300)\n",
        "    plt.show()\n",
        "\n",
        "for label in ['fake', 'real']:\n",
        "    plot_top_ngrams(df[df['label'] == label]['content'], n=2, label_category=label)"

      "source": [
        "## 3.7 TF-IDF Feature Matrix Construction\n",
        "\n",
        "**TF-IDF (Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency)** is the standard numerical text representation for document classification. It assigns each term a weight reflecting how distinctive it is to a specific article relative to the broader corpus:\n",
        "\n",
        "- **TF (Term Frequency):** How often a term appears in a given article\n",
        "- **IDF (Inverse Document Frequency):** A penalty for terms that appear across many articles — common terms like `said` or `people` receive low IDF weights, while distinctive terms receive high weights\n",
        "\n",
        "**Configuration decisions:**\n",
        "- `max_features=20,000` — retains the 20,000 most discriminative terms/phrases, balancing expressiveness with memory efficiency\n",
        "- `ngram_range=(1,2)` — includes both single words (unigrams) and two-word phrases (bigrams), capturing co-occurrence patterns that single words miss (e.g., `white house` vs `white` + `house` separately)"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": null,
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "Bvh4QojWD-ja",
        "outputId": "5cae923e-b006-48af-b5a0-d720113969f7"
      },
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stdout",
          "text": [
            "✓ TF-IDF matrix constructed.\n",
            "  Shape: 826 documents x 20,000 features\n",
            "  Matrix type: csr_matrix (memory-efficient sparse format)\n"
          ]
        }
      ],
      "source": [
        "# ── Build the TF-IDF feature matrix ──────────────────────────────────────────\n",
        "tfidf   = TfidfVectorizer(max_features=20_000, ngram_range=(1, 2))\n",
        "X_tfidf = tfidf.fit_transform(df['content'])\n",
        "\n",
        "print(\"✓ TF-IDF matrix constructed.\")\n",
        "print(f\"  Shape: {X_tfidf.shape[0]:,} documents x {X_tfidf.shape[1]:,} features\")\n",
        "print(f\"  Matrix type: {type(X_tfidf).__name__} (memory-efficient sparse format)\")"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "p2KdWueQD-jb"
      },
      "source": [
        "**TF-IDF matrix confirmed: 826 documents × 20,000 features.** The sparse format stores only non-zero values — critical for a 20,000-feature matrix where each document contains only a tiny fraction of the full vocabulary. This keeps memory usage manageable while preserving full feature expressiveness.\n",
        "\n",
        "---"
      ]

        "## 3.9 Label Encoding and Train-Test Split\n",
        "\n",
        "`LabelEncoder` maps string labels (`fake` → 0, `real` → 1) to integers for scikit-learn compatibility. We split **90% training / 10% test** using `stratify=y` to preserve the exact 50/50 class distribution in both partitions.\n",
        "\n",
        "**Why 90/10 split?** With only 826 total samples after downsampling, a 90/10 split maximises training data (743 samples) while still reserving a meaningful test set (83 samples — approximately 41 per class). A larger test set would leave too few samples for stable model training."
      ]
    },
    {

        "# ── Encode string labels to integers ─────────────────────────────────────────\n",
        "le = LabelEncoder()\n",

        "print(f\"✓ Label encoding: {dict(zip(le.classes_, le.transform(le.classes_)))}\")\n",

        "X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(\n",

        ")\n",

        "print(f\"  Training set : {X_train.shape[0]:,} samples  ({X_train.shape[0]/X.shape[0]*100:.1f}%) — {X_train.shape[1]:,} features\")\n",
        "print(f\"  Test set     : {X_test.shape[0]:,} samples  ({X_test.shape[0]/X.shape[0]*100:.1f}%) — sealed hold-out, not used during training\")"
      ]

The 83-sample test set is sealed — it will not be touched until each model's final evaluation. No scaler is applied here; TF-IDF features are already in [0,1] range, and the two numerical features have bounded natural scales.\n",
        "\n",

      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "K-yX9oq6D-jf"
      },
      "source": [
        "---\n",
        "# STEP 4: MODEL DEVELOPMENT & EVALUATION\n",
        "\n",
        "With the preprocessed, balanced, split feature matrix ready, we train and evaluate five classifiers of increasing complexity. All models use `random_state=42` for reproducibility and are evaluated on the same sealed 83-sample test set.\n",
        "\n",
        "| # | Model | Type | Rationale for Inclusion |\n",
        "|---|-------|------|------------------------|\n",
        "| 1 | Logistic Regression | Linear baseline | Interpretable; L2 regularisation handles high-dimensional TF-IDF well |\n",
        "| 2 | Support Vector Classifier (SVC) | Kernel-based | Strong theoretical guarantees; tested with default RBF kernel |\n",
        "| 3 | Decision Tree | Single non-linear tree | Interpretable splits; serves as a mid-complexity reference |\n",
        "| 4 | Random Forest | Bagging ensemble | Reduces Decision Tree variance via aggregation over 100 trees |\n",
        "| 5 | XGBoost | Boosting ensemble | Sequential residual correction; state-of-the-art on structured classification |\n",
        "\n",
        "**Evaluation metrics:**\n",
        "- **Accuracy** — overall correctness (reliable here due to 1:1 class balance)\n",
        "- **Precision** — of all articles flagged as fake/real, what fraction are correct?\n",
        "- **Recall** — of all actual fake/real articles, what fraction does the model catch?\n",
        "- **F1-Score** — harmonic mean of Precision and Recall; penalises extreme imbalances between the two\n",
        "- **ROC-AUC** — threshold-independent discrimination ability; 1.0 = perfect, 0.5 = random\n",
        "\n",
        "---"
      ]
    },
    {

        "- The confusion matrix reveals a **severe class bias**: the model classifies the majority of articles as `fake` — achieving very high fake recall (0.88) but catastrophically low real recall (0.49), meaning it correctly identifies only 49% of actual real articles. It is essentially defaulting to the majority class from the pre-balancing distribution.\n",
        "- The default **RBF kernel** is the root cause. The RBF kernel computes pairwise Euclidean distances in a 20,002-dimensional space — an ill-suited geometric operation for sparse TF-IDF matrices where most dimensions are zero. A `kernel='linear'` SVC would behave similarly to Logistic Regression on this representation. This is noted as an untested configuration for future work.\n",
        "- The macro-average F1 of 0.67 confirms the model is not achieving balanced performance across classes.\n",

        "## 4.6 Baseline Model Comparison — ROC-AUC\n",
        "\n",
        "ROC-AUC quantifies the probability that a randomly chosen fake article is scored higher than a randomly chosen real article. It evaluates model performance across all classification thresholds simultaneously — making it robust to the threshold choice and more informative than a single accuracy figure."
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",

        "---\n",
        "# STEP 5: HYPERPARAMETER TUNING\n",
        "\n",
        "The baseline models used default configurations — a fair benchmark, but suboptimal settings. We now apply **GridSearchCV with 5-fold cross-validation** to both selected models, using **ROC-AUC** as the optimisation objective.\n",
        "\n",
        "**Why ROC-AUC as the tuning objective?** Accuracy optimisation on a balanced dataset would produce similar results, but ROC-AUC rewards models that rank articles correctly across all thresholds — a more robust and practically useful criterion for a content screening tool where the operating threshold may need to be adjusted based on deployment context (e.g., stricter thresholds for high-stakes editorial decisions).\n",
        "\n",
        "**Important context on sample size:** With only 743 training samples, 5-fold CV uses ~595 samples for training and ~148 for validation per fold. This is a small dataset by NLP standards — the CV AUC estimates will have non-trivial variance, and results should be interpreted with appropriate caution.\n",
        "\n",
        "---"
      ]

      "source": [
        "## 5.1 Tuning Utility Function\n",
        "\n",
        "A reusable `tune_and_evaluate_model()` function encapsulates the complete GridSearchCV workflow. This ensures identical tuning conditions for both models and eliminates code duplication."
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": null,
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "SYaIbAUHD-jt",
        "outputId": "d8e7e553-16c3-43f7-b131-f10ecdbcb734"
      },
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stdout",
          "text": [
            "✓ tune_and_evaluate_model() function defined.\n"
          ]
        }
      ],
      "source": [
        "# ── Reusable GridSearchCV tuning and evaluation function ─────────────────────\n",
        "def tune_and_evaluate_model(model_class, param_grid, name, X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, cv=5):\n",
        "\n",
        "    print(f\"\\n── Tuning: {name}  |  GridSearchCV  |  cv={cv}  |  scoring=roc_auc ──────────\")\n",
        "\n",
        "    # ── GridSearchCV: exhaustive search over param_grid with 5-fold CV ────────\n",
        "    grid = GridSearchCV(model_class, param_grid, cv=cv, scoring='roc_auc', n_jobs=-1)\n",
        "    grid.fit(X_train, y_train)\n",
        "\n",
        "    best_model = grid.best_estimator_\n",
        "    print(f\"  Best Parameters : {grid.best_params_}\")\n",
        "    print(f\"  Best CV AUC     : {grid.best_score_:.4f}\")\n",
        "\n",
        "    # ── Test set predictions ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n",
        "    y_pred       = best_model.predict(X_test)\n",
        "    y_pred_proba = best_model.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]\n",
        "\n",
        "    # ── Metrics ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n",
        "    print(f\"\\n  Accuracy Score  : {accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred):.4f}\")\n",
        "    print(\"\\n  Classification Report:\")\n",
        "    print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred, target_names=['fake', 'real']))\n",
        "\n",
        "    # ── Confusion matrix ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n",
        "    plt.figure(figsize=(5, 4))\n",
        "    sns.heatmap(confusion_matrix(y_test, y_pred), annot=True, fmt='d', cmap='Greens',\n",
        "                xticklabels=['fake', 'real'], yticklabels=['fake', 'real'])\n",
        "    plt.title(f'{name} — Confusion Matrix', fontweight='bold')\n",
        "    plt.xlabel('Predicted')\n",
        "    plt.ylabel('Actual')\n",
        "    plt.tight_layout()\n",
        "    plt.savefig(f'{name.replace(\" \", \"_\")}_confusion_matrix.png')\n",
        "    plt.show()\n",
        "\n",
        "    # ── ROC data ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n",
        "    fpr_vals, tpr_vals, _ = roc_curve(y_test, y_pred_proba)\n",
        "    auc_val = auc(fpr_vals, tpr_vals)\n",
        "\n",
        "    return {\n",
        "        'model': best_model, 'name': name, 'y_pred': y_pred,\n",
        "        'accuracy': accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred),\n",
        "        'best_params': grid.best_params_,\n",
        "        'fpr': fpr_vals, 'tpr': tpr_vals, 'auc': auc_val\n",
        "    }\n",
        "\n",
        "print(\"✓ tune_and_evaluate_model() function defined.\")"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "M6Ogk65YD-ju"

        "---\n",
        "## 5.6 Feature Importance — Top Lexical Drivers of Fake vs Real News\n",
        "\n",
        "The Tuned Logistic Regression's coefficient vector is a transparent window into what the model has learned. Each coefficient directly quantifies how strongly a term pushes a prediction toward `real` (positive coefficient) or `fake` (negative coefficient). We analyse the Top 20 features by absolute coefficient magnitude — the terms with the strongest discriminative power in either direction.\n",
        "\n",
        "Note: This analysis uses the Tuned Logistic Regression specifically because it provides directly interpretable coefficients. The Tuned XGBoost is the better overall model, but its feature importances (Gini reduction) are less directly interpretable as directional signals."

        "# ── Extract and rank Top 20 features from the Tuned LR model ─────────────────\n",
        "coefficients        = tuned_log_reg_model.coef_[0]\n",
        "tfidf_feature_names = tfidf.get_feature_names_out()\n",
        "all_feature_names   = list(tfidf_feature_names) + ['word_count', 'sentiment']\n",
        "\n",
        "feature_importance  = pd.Series(coefficients, index=all_feature_names)\n",
        "top_20              = feature_importance.abs().sort_values(ascending=False).head(20)\n",

      "source": [
        "## 6.2 Key Findings from the Data\n",
        "\n",
        "**A. The Dataset Requires Careful Label Engineering — Not a Simple Binary Problem**\n",
        "The raw `type` column contains 8 categories with an 88.4% dominance of `bs` articles. A naive binary split would produce a 29.8:1 imbalance (fake:real), making accuracy meaningless. The label mapping decision — treating `bias` as the \"real\" proxy — is a pragmatic but imperfect solution acknowledged throughout this report.\n",
        "\n",
        "**B. Downsampling Creates a Small but Balanced Training Set**\n",
        "After mapping and balancing, 826 records remain (413 per class). This is a small dataset by NLP standards. The models trained on 743 samples achieve meaningful accuracy (up to 86.75%), confirming that TF-IDF + bigrams provide sufficient signal density even on small corpora.\n",
        "\n",
        "**C. XGBoost's Sequential Boosting Outperforms Logistic Regression on Small Datasets**\n",
        "The 4.82 percentage point gap between Tuned XGBoost (86.75%) and Logistic Regression (79.52%) is notable. On this 826-record dataset, gradient boosting's ability to incrementally correct residuals across 200 shallow trees provides a meaningful advantage over a single linear model.\n",
        "\n",
        "**D. SVC with RBF Kernel is Unsuitable for Sparse TF-IDF Representations**\n",
        "The RBF kernel SVC achieved only 68.67% accuracy — it computes pairwise Euclidean distances in a 20,002-dimensional sparse space, which is geometrically ill-suited. A linear kernel SVC would be expected to perform comparably to Logistic Regression.\n",
        "\n",
        "**E. Feature Importance Reveals Both Signal and Dataset Fragility**\n",
        "The dominant REAL-signal term (`trump`, coeff = 6.25) is 2× stronger than any other feature and likely reflects source-specific writing patterns in the `bias` category rather than a universal indicator of real news. This is a dataset-specific artifact that may not generalise to new data.\n",
        "\n",
        "---"
      ]

        "## 6.3 Actionable Business Recommendations\n",
        "\n",
        "---\n",
        "\n",
        "### Recommendation 1 — Deploy the Tuned XGBoost as a Real-Time Content Screening Service\n",
        "**Priority: 🔴 HIGH**\n",
        "\n",
        "**Evidence:** AUC = 0.9393, Accuracy = 86.75%, F1 = 0.87 (both classes). The model is serialised and verified.\n",
        "\n",
        "**Action:** Wrap `tuned_xgboost_fake_news.joblib` and the TF-IDF vectoriser in a REST API endpoint. For any submitted article (`title` + `text`), the endpoint returns: (a) binary classification (`fake` / `real`), (b) probability confidence score, and (c) a confidence flag for borderline predictions (probability between 0.40–0.60). Pair with the Tuned Logistic Regression as an explainability layer — use its top coefficients to surface the specific terms driving each flag.\n",
        "\n",
        "---\n",
        "\n",
        "### Recommendation 2 — Re-Engineer the Label Taxonomy with Domain Experts\n",
        "**Priority: 🔴 HIGH**\n",
        "\n",
        "**Evidence:** The current `bias` → `real` mapping is a proxy, not a ground truth. Treating partisan-but-real reporting as \"real news\" introduces class noise that dilutes model performance. This is the single largest addressable limitation in the current pipeline.\n",
        "\n",
        "**Action:** Engage TruthLens journalism researchers to review the 8 original categories and define a principled, application-appropriate mapping. Consider a three-class model (`fake`, `biased`, `credible`) rather than forcing a binary split.\n",
        "\n",
        "---\n",
        "\n",
        "### Recommendation 3 — Incorporate Source-Level Metadata Features\n",
        "**Priority: 🟠 MEDIUM**\n",
        "\n",
        "**Evidence:** The original dataset contains `site_url` (source domain), `published` (timestamp), `spam_score`, `domain_rank`, and engagement metrics (`likes`, `shares`, `comments`) that were excluded from the current pipeline. Domain-level credibility signals (e.g., known satire sites, fact-checked outlets) are among the strongest predictors of misinformation in the published literature.\n",
        "\n",
        "**Action:** In the next training cycle, retain `site_url` → extract domain → encode domain trust tier. Retain `published` → extract hour and day-of-week. Include `spam_score` and `domain_rank` as direct numerical features. Expected improvement: 2–5 AUC points based on comparable studies.\n",
        "\n",
        "---\n",
        "\n",
        "### Recommendation 4 — Expand the Training Data to Increase Robustness\n",
        "**Priority: 🟠 MEDIUM**\n",
        "\n",
        "**Evidence:** The final training set of 743 samples is very small by NLP standards. The CV AUC of 0.8987 vs test AUC of 0.9393 suggests the model generalises reasonably, but variance on this sample size is non-trivial. The downsampling from 12,307 `fake` articles to 413 discards 96.6% of available fake training data.\n",
        "\n",
        "**Action:** Collect additional verified `real` news articles to expand the minority class rather than discarding the majority. Target a minimum of 5,000 balanced samples (2,500 per class) for the next training cycle.\n",
        "\n",
        "---"
      ]

      "source": [
        "## 6.4 Limitations and Next Steps\n",
        "\n",
        "| Limitation | Impact | Recommended Mitigation |\n",
        "|-----------|--------|------------------------|\n",
        "| **Imperfect binary mapping** | `bias` ≠ real news; classification boundary is fuzzy | Engage domain experts to redesign the label taxonomy |\n",
        "| **Small training set (743 samples)** | High variance in CV estimates; model may not generalise well to new article styles | Expand the real-news corpus; use data augmentation techniques |\n",
        "| **Metadata excluded** | `site_url`, `spam_score`, `domain_rank`, engagement signals unused | Retain and engineer source-level features in next pipeline version |\n",
        "| **Static TF-IDF vocabulary** | New terminology (new political figures, events, neologisms) is invisible | Explore contextual embeddings (BERT, RoBERTa) for dynamic vocabulary |\n",
        "| **US political domain** | Dataset is concentrated on 2015–2016 US election coverage | Augment with international, multi-topic, multi-year data |\n",
        "| **Dominant coefficient fragility** | `trump` coeff = 6.25 may reflect source style, not real news signal | Monitor feature drift; retrain quarterly with new labelled data |\n",
        "| **Default RBF SVC untested as linear** | `kernel='linear'` SVC not evaluated | Include linear SVC as an additional baseline in future benchmarks |\n",
        "\n",
